adc.label: 模数转换器（ADC）
adc.about: 把模拟信号按固定满量程采样成数字样本。
adc.about_en: Samples an analog signal into digital samples at a fixed full scale.
adc.doc:
A sampling ADC with one input and a fixed full scale: where an analog
signal becomes samples.

``in`` takes the analog signal, ``out`` gives its sample stream at the rate asked of it (its
own ``rate`` when nobody says: a probe). A frame is made in this order:

1. the signal is evaluated at the request's instants — at the tuning the request names, when
   it names one (a receiver's IF depends on where its oscillator is);
2. the noise of the analog chain ahead becomes samples: the cascaded noise figure and gain of
   the ``RfStage`` blocks found walking the wiring upstream, as white noise of that density
   over the Nyquist band, kT0·F·G·(rate/2) into ``impedance``, drawn from the request's random
   stream. A chain that declares no noise figure adds none;
3. the converter's own noise (``noise_lsb_rms``), from a stream of its own;
4. the sum is quantized to ``bits`` over ±``full_scale`` and clipped there.

The samples are the codes, kept in volts (as the scope's): the format says how many bits
and what one code step is worth. ``bits`` 0 does not quantize (and cannot clip). The request's
interval is the real one — the block that starts the read holds the clock and its error.

amplitude_level.label: 幅度与偏置
amplitude_level.about: 按仪表的定义把 1 Vpp 波形缩放到设定的幅度并加上偏置。
amplitude_level.about_en: Scales a 1 Vpp waveform to the set amplitude and adds the offset, as the instrument defines them.
amplitude_level.doc:
The amplitude and offset of a 1 Vpp waveform, as the instrument defines them.

``amplitude`` is in ``unit``: VPP, VPK, VRMS (through each function's peak-to-RMS ratio: sine
2√2, square and pulse 2, ramp 2√3 Vpp per Vrms) or DBM (the power into the load setting:
Vrms = √(10^(dBm/10) · 1 mW · R)). The level is what a load of ``load_setting`` ohms would see
behind ``output``'s impedance, so the EMF is raised by (R + Z) / R; ``inf``, or ``hiz_from`` ohms
and more, is high-Z: the level is the open-circuit voltage and dBm is referred to
``dbm_hiz_ohms`` (50 Ω, the usual convention when the load is unknown).

``vpp_min`` / ``vpp_max`` bound the amplitude as volts peak-to-peak into the load setting, the
one physical limit a source has: a write in any unit is converted and checked, refusing
with -222; a change of the waveform or the load setting that would leave the range is refused
with -221. Switching the unit converts the value, so the output does not move (a real source's
``VOLT:UNIT``); there is no dBm expression of 0 Vpp, so that switch is refused with -221.

arb_segments.label: 任意波存储
arb_segments.about: 任意波发生器的波形段存储，按采样率经零阶保持 DAC 循环播放。
arb_segments.about_en: Waveform segments of an arbitrary generator, played in a loop through a zero-order-hold DAC.
arb_segments.doc:
An arbitrary waveform generator's waveform memory: segments of signed DAC codes, played in a
loop at the sample frequency through a zero-order-hold DAC (the sin(x)/x roll-off of the
spectrum). A segment is defined (``define``, ``define_new``, write-only variants), filled in
pieces at a sample offset (``data``), listed (``catalog``), named, commented and deleted.

Model limits: one segment plays, ``play``; a segment's length is a multiple of ``granularity`` and
at least ``min_length``; the segments together hold at most ``max_samples`` (-225 beyond it).
A write past a segment's length is -223 (too much data), a segment that is not defined or a
number outside the code range is -222; reading back a write-only segment is -221 (the manual says
only that it cannot be read back). Sequencing, markers and interpolated I/Q modes are not modeled.

arb_table.label: 任意波表
arb_table.about: 按设定采样率播放的波形表，点间线性插值。
arb_table.about_en: A waveform table played at the set sample rate, linearly interpolated.
arb_table.doc:
An arbitrary waveform: a table played at ``rate`` samples per second, linearly interpolated.

The output is periodic with fundamental ``rate / N``. Linear interpolation between samples is a
convolution with a triangle, so harmonic k carries ``X[k mod N] / N · sinc²(k / N)``: the
spectrum is exact, not sampled. Harmonics are kept up to ``max_lines``.

awg_modulator.label: 波形调制
awg_modulator.about: 函数发生器的调制，位于波形合成与幅度/偏置之间。
awg_modulator.about_en: A function generator's modulation, between waveform synthesis and amplitude/offset.

cal_output.label: 校准输出选择
cal_output.about: 选择前面板输出端口送出的信号（:CALibrate:OUTPut）。
cal_output.about_en: Chooses the signal a front-panel output port carries (:CALibrate:OUTPut).
cal_output.doc:
The signal a front-panel output port carries, chosen by ``:CALibrate:OUTPut`` (source block).

``selection`` is the stored selection (a word, ``DC`` followed by ``,<level>`` for the DC form).
``port`` says which connector this is: on ``cal`` the DC word carries the commanded level
(±``dc_max``); the ``aux`` connector's DC word is the fixed ``zero_level`` (the guide: AUX OUT's
DC is the ZERO level, −440 mV). ZERO and ONE are constant levels, PROB the probe-compensation
square (750 Hz), MHZ97 / MHZ7_5 clock squares. TOUT (trigger-event pulse, needs the high-bandwidth
trigger option) and the DPUL / NDPUL pulses are not modeled: those outputs idle at ``zero_level``.
``rise`` (FAST or SLOW) limits the edges' bandwidth on the ``aux`` connector. Levels other than
ZERO's and the 750 Hz are SimuBench values, not from the guide. The enable and the output
impedance are the downstream ``output_stage``'s.

calibration_store.label: 校准存储
calibration_store.about: 按测量条件保存校准系数和校准记录。
calibration_store.about_en: Keeps calibration coefficients by measurement context, and the calibration ledger.
calibration_store.doc:
Calibration coefficients keyed by the measurement context, and the calibration ledger.

A measuring core references the store with ``store: <this component's name>`` and reads its
reading as ``(raw − offset[key]) × gain[key]``; a key never adjusted gives gain 1 and offset 0.
The key comes from the ``key`` parameter, one entry per key dimension:

* ``$path`` - the value of that instrument state (e.g. ``$sense.function``);
* ``component.param`` - that component's parameter; for the calibrated core itself,
  ``function`` is the function of the measurement being made and ``range`` the range actually
  in use (the auto-chosen one included), e.g. ``[meter.function, meter.range]``.

``adjust`` (a reference of 0 adjusts the zero, anything else the gain) checks the core's raw
input against the reference first: the deviation must stay within ``tolerance`` of the
reference (of ``max(|reference|, 1)`` for the zero, where the reference itself is 0). A failed
check pushes the calibration error (702 by default) and replies ``fail_reply``. Adjusted
coefficients take effect at once and become permanent when ``store`` commits them; whether an
un-stored adjustment survives ``*RST`` is ``volatile_until_store``. The ledger (``count``,
``date``, ``time``, ``string``) and the security ``code`` are never touched by ``*RST``.
``secured`` and ``value`` may be bound to instrument state (``$cal.secured``); set through the
ops they write that state back, so the store follows the instrument's own variables.

calibrator_control.label: 校准源输出控制
calibrator_control.about: 校准源的工作/待机、输出阻抗和过载跳回待机。
calibrator_control.about_en: A calibrator's operate/standby, output impedance and overload trip to standby.
calibrator_control.doc:
The calibrator's output control: ``operate`` (standby disconnects the terminal),
``z_out``, ``i_max`` (the overload trip back to standby with ``overload_error``) and
``standby_above`` (a change of the output to or from above it returns to standby). It drives
the setpoint block's signal onto the electrical terminal.

calibrator_output.label: 校准源输出
calibrator_output.about: 校准源的设定值与输出控制合在一个块里。
calibrator_output.about_en: A calibrator's setpoint and output control in one block.
calibrator_output.doc:
A calibrator's setpoint and output control in one block: ``function`` (DCV | ACV),
``level`` (V; RMS for ACV), ``frequency`` (Hz; 0 for DCV), ``operate``, ``z_out``, ``i_max``,
``settle`` (s, or a table per function), ``standby_above`` (V), and the hidden
``gain_error_ppm`` / ``offset`` of the output stage. The same behaviour as
``calibrator_setpoint`` + ``calibrator_control``, for definitions written before the
split.

The settings are bound to instrument state (``function: $out.function`` ...); the commands
write the state and the component follows. ``settle`` is taken from the table by the target
function when it is a dict (``{DCV: 1.0, ACV: 2.0}``).

calibrator_setpoint.label: 校准源设定
calibrator_setpoint.about: 校准源的功能、电平、频率与量程生成。
calibrator_setpoint.about_en: A calibrator's function, level, frequency and range generation.
calibrator_setpoint.doc:
The calibrator's setpoint and range generation: ``function`` (DCV | ACV), ``level``
(V; RMS for ACV), ``frequency``, ``settle`` (s, or a table per function) and the hidden
``gain_error_ppm`` / ``offset``. Its ``out`` is the signal the output control drives onto the
terminal; it settles in virtual time when the control operates it.

clock_recovery.label: 时钟恢复
clock_recovery.about: 从数据中恢复时钟，作为无独立时钟的采样示波器的触发。
clock_recovery.about_en: Recovers a clock from the data, the trigger of a sampling scope with no separate clock.
clock_recovery.doc:
A clock recovered from the data on ``in``: the trigger of a sampling scope with no separate
clock. It locks when the data's symbol rate lies within ``lock_range`` (relative) of the nominal
``rate`` and between ``min_rate`` and ``max_rate``; the pattern's length comes with it (the
repetition rate's multiple), which pattern lock uses. The symbol rate is read from the pattern's
spectrum (:func:`symbol_multiple`); when the spectrum does not show it, the multiple of the
repetition rate nearest the nominal rate is taken. The loop is not simulated: ``loop_bandwidth``
is kept and answered, the recovered clock follows the data exactly (no tracking error, no
transfer of jitter).

coax_cable.label: 同轴线缆
coax_cable.about: 一段短同轴线：只有很小的串联电阻，不计延时和反射。
coax_cable.about_en: A short cable: a small series resistance, no delay or reflections.
coax_cable.doc:
A short cable: a small series resistance (no delay or reflections).

``r_skin_1mhz`` adds the skin effect: a series impedance ``r_skin_1mhz * sqrt(f / 1 MHz) * (1 + j)``
(resistance and internal reactance rise together with the square root of frequency), which
makes a 50 Ω path lose a little more at higher frequencies and a square wave settle slowly
after each edge. A lumped model, valid while the cable is short against the wavelength.

counter_core.label: 计数核心
counter_core.about: 在闸门时间内测频率、周期、累计计数和时间间隔。
counter_core.about_en: Measures frequency, period, totalize and time interval over the gate.
counter_core.doc:
The counting core: frequency, period, totalize and time interval over the gate.

Frequency and period use reciprocal counting over the events inside the gate, so a fast
timebase reads low by ε (the same convention as the spectrum analyzer's display); totalize
reports the crossings inside the gate; time interval is measured between the first event on
channel A and the next on channel B, plus each channel's trigger error (normal, seeded by the
virtual instant, so two readings at one instant agree).

counter_gate.label: 闸门
counter_gate.about: 计数器的闸门时间与闸门源，以及时基产生的真实时长。
counter_gate.about_en: The counter's gate time and source, and the true duration the timebase produces.
counter_gate.doc:
The gate: its time and source, and the true duration the timebase produces. A fast
timebase makes the instrument's second short, so the gate lasts ``T / (1 + ε)`` of true time.

counter_input.label: 计数器输入
counter_input.about: 一个输入通道：阻抗、交直流耦合、触发电平和灵敏度。
counter_input.about_en: One input channel: impedance, AC/DC coupling, trigger level and sensitivity.
counter_input.doc:
One input channel: impedance (1 MΩ or 50 Ω) at the pin, AC/DC coupling, the trigger
level and the sensitivity (the smallest peak-to-peak amplitude the channel counts; below it the
signal is rejected as noise).

counter_statistics.label: 统计
counter_statistics.about: 对测量结果求平均、最小、最大和标准差。
counter_statistics.about_en: Mean, minimum, maximum and standard deviation of the measurements taken.
counter_statistics.doc:
The statistics block: the measurements taken, and their mean, minimum, maximum and
standard deviation (sample standard deviation, n − 1).

counter_timebase.label: 计数器时基
counter_timebase.about: 把参考时钟变成仪表的时间刻度，含插值器的单次分辨率。
counter_timebase.about_en: Turns the reference clock into the instrument's time scale, with the interpolator's resolution.
counter_timebase.doc:
The counter's timebase: the reference clock
turned into the instrument's time scale. A timestamp is the true instant on that scale — a fast
clock reads time long by its error ε — with the interpolator's single-shot resolution (normal,
seeded by the instant, so a repeated reading agrees).

``gap_free`` is continuous measurement without dead time: each frequency reading spans from the
previous gate's last edge to this gate's last edge, so adjacent readings share their boundary
edge and the readings times their spans add up exactly to the edges counted (the 53230A's
gap-free mode; without it each gate measures its own first-to-last edge span).

curve_buffer.label: 曲线缓冲
curve_buffer.about: 按采样率把迹线记入数据点，可开始、暂停、继续和清空。
curve_buffer.about_en: Records traces at a rate into bins, with start, pause, resume and reset.
curve_buffer.doc:
Traces sampled at a rate into bins, with start, pause, resume and reset.

The SR830's data storage: two traces (the CH1/CH2 displays), 62.5 mHz – 512 Hz or one point
per trigger, single shot or loop, ``TRCA?``/``TRCB?``/``TRCL?`` reading k points from bin j.

daq_backplane.label: 主机背板
daq_backplane.about: 数据采集主机的插槽和已装的模块。
daq_backplane.about_en: The data-acquisition mainframe's slots and installed modules.
daq_backplane.doc:
The mainframe's slots and installed modules.

The modules named here are what a SCPI channel number refers to: ``101`` is channel 1 of the
module in slot 1 (``slot_stride`` is the SCPI slot field, 100). First wave: the 34970A has
three slots and one 34901A in slot 1; a channel of an empty slot does not exist. The scan
table and the multiplexer card check their channels against it.

data_file.label: 数据文件
data_file.about: 把测量数据（读数存储或通道记录）写到仪表的驱动器上。
data_file.about_en: Writes measurement data (reading memory or a channel's record) to the instrument's drives.
data_file.doc:
Write measurement data to a file on the instrument's drives: the reading memory
(MMEMory:STORe:DATA RDG_STORE) or a channel's record (:DISK:SAVE:WAVeform).

Readings are written as the buffer's queries write them, one column per scanned channel
(``column_header``, ``{channel}``) and one row per sweep, separated by ``separator`` (a
setting: COMMa, SEMicolon or TAB); readings without a channel go in one column. A reading file
whose extension is in ``refused_extensions`` (the DAQ970A's binary ``.dat``) is refused with
``refused_error``. Waveforms: CSV, TSV and TXT are ``time,volts`` lines (``header`` adds
``key,value`` lines first), BIN is the Keysight binary file; INTernal, H5, H5INt and MATlab are
refused. Model limits: the text layout and its header lines are SimuBench's (the guide does not
give them); only channel sources, one record per file (no segments, no ALL).

dc_supply.label: 直流电源
dc_supply.about: 带输出电阻的固定直流源（台式电源或电池），对地输出。
dc_supply.about_en: A fixed DC source with an output resistance (a bench supply or a battery), to ground.
dc_supply.doc: A fixed DC source with an output resistance (a bench supply or a battery), to ground.

dmm_adc.label: 万用表 A/D
dmm_adc.about: 万用表的 A/D 转换：位数、积分时间（NPLC）、分辨率、校准与读数。
dmm_adc.about_en: The DMM's A/D: digits, NPLC reading time, resolution, calibration and the reading.
dmm_adc.doc:
The A/D: digits, NPLC reading time, resolution, calibration and the reading.

It reads the conditioning block's raw value, applies the calibration coefficients and the
resolution quantization, and turns a reading beyond ``overrange`` × full scale into
``overload_value``. Calibration: with ``store`` naming a ``calibration_store`` component the
reading is corrected with the store's per-key coefficients and the
``cal_*`` operations delegate to it; without a store the single legacy coefficient set below
applies. The component is the instrument's sampler.

dmm_conditioning.label: 信号调理
dmm_conditioning.about: 万用表的功能、量程、交流滤波及模拟误差。
dmm_conditioning.about_en: The DMM's function, ranges, AC filter and analog errors.
dmm_conditioning.doc:
Signal conditioning: function, ranges and the AC filter, and the analog errors.

DC (mean) and true-rms AC of the signal on its input; AC is the rms of the lines above
``ac_low`` Hz (the AC path's coupling), each weighted by the true-rms converter's high-frequency
response when ``ac_high`` is given: a Butterworth magnitude ``1/√(1 + (f/ac_high)^(2·order))``
with its −3 dB point at ``ac_high`` Hz, so lines past the meter's bandwidth read low; the ACI function
has its own point ``ac_high_current`` (current is measured through a shunt: far less bandwidth than
voltage, #1279). The measurement path has a hidden gain error (ppm) and
offset (V), the instrument's own errors; the ADC's calibration coefficients correct them::

    raw     = true × (1 + gain_error_ppm·1e-6) + offset
    reading = (raw − cal.offset) × cal.gain

With ``ranges`` the meter ranges: the function's full-scale values,
a manual ``range`` (a value the range must be able to measure; the smallest fitting range is
used, as SCPI prescribes) and ``autorange`` (the range follows the true value; above
``autorange_up`` × full scale or below ``autorange_down`` × it, the smallest range that fits
the value is taken). The hidden errors may be one number (every range alike) or per function
and range: ``{DC: {0.1: 8, 1: 3}, AC: 60}``.

dmm_input_terminal.label: 万用表输入端子
dmm_input_terminal.about: 万用表的电气输入及其对地阻抗。
dmm_input_terminal.about_en: The DMM's electrical input and its impedance to ground.
dmm_input_terminal.doc:
The DMM's input terminals: the electrical input and its impedance to ground.

``pin`` is the instrument's electrical terminal (a definition exposes it as ``IN``); ``out``
carries the measured signal on to the conditioning block. With ``z_in`` the terminal models its
own input stage, so the resistance enters the bench circuit: ``z_in_high`` on the
``high_z_ranges`` when ``high_z`` is set. Without ``z_in`` the terminal is a pass-through and
an ``input_port`` in front owns the electrical side.

The high-impedance choice follows the range in use, which the conditioning block knows; the
terminal references it (``conditioning``).

eload_input.label: 负载输入级
eload_input.about: 电子负载的输入端子和开关，接入电路的元件。
eload_input.about_en: The electronic load's input terminal and switch, the element in the circuit.
eload_input.doc:
The load's input terminal and switch: the element that stamps the circuit.

It owns the ``in`` port; with the input off (or a protection trip latched) it is an open
circuit. Otherwise it stamps what the mode loop decided: a current sink (CC/CP), a resistance
(CR or the CC knee) or a voltage clamp (CV). ``c_in`` adds the input capacitance to ground.

eload_meter.label: 负载测量
eload_meter.about: 电子负载的电压、电流和功率测量。
eload_meter.about_en: The electronic load's voltage, current and power measurement.
eload_meter.doc:
The load's V/I/P measurement. The readings keep the ``load.*`` keys the front
panel uses; the input stage supplies the solved values.

eload_mode_loop.label: 负载模式环
eload_mode_loop.about: 电子负载的工作模式：恒流、恒压、恒阻或恒功率。
eload_mode_loop.about_en: The electronic load's operating mode: CC, CV, CR or CP.
eload_mode_loop.doc:
The static function and the operating-point mode: CC, CV, CR or CP.

``function`` names the static mode; the setpoint belongs to it (``current``, ``voltage``,
``resistance`` or ``power``). ``von`` is the starting voltage: below it a CC (or CP) load does
not sink. ``slew`` (A/µs) limits how fast the CC current follows a setpoint change; the ramp is
evaluated at the current virtual instant, so a later reading sees the intermediate current.

The mode loop is piecewise: :meth:`update_mode` reads the solved input voltage
and the present sink current and chooses ``("open"|"i"|"r"|"v", value)`` — a current sink, a
resistance or a voltage clamp (CV mode). The CP hysteresis (I = P/V) is iterated to a
self-consistent point.

Model options (defaults keep the old behaviour): ``von_latch`` keeps a load that has
once seen the input above Von sinking below it until the input switches off; ``slew_rise`` /
``slew_fall`` give rising and falling CC steps their own rates; ``*_ranges`` declare a
setting's ranges as ``[low, high]`` pairs — the bound ``*_range`` setting is moved to the
smallest range that holds the value written, and a setpoint outside the new range is brought
to its nearest edge (the B&K 8600 rule: CURR:RANG 30 selects the 240 A range).

eload_power_stage.label: 负载功率级
eload_power_stage.about: 电子负载的工作范围：恒流拐点、电流与功率能力。
eload_power_stage.about_en: The load's operating envelope: CC knee, current and power capability.
eload_power_stage.doc:
The sink's operating envelope: the CC knee, the current and power capability.

In constant current mode the load cannot go below its minimum operating resistance ``r_min``:
below the knee voltage (``r_min`` × the set current) it behaves as that resistance instead of
the current sink. ``i_max`` and ``p_max`` cap every mode (the constant-power envelope), so a
CC setpoint above the capability is power-limited rather than drawn.

eload_protection.label: 负载保护
eload_protection.about: 过压、过流、过功率保护的门限和跳闸锁存。
eload_protection.about_en: Over-voltage, over-current and over-power thresholds and the trip latch.
eload_protection.doc:
OVP / OCP / OPP protection: thresholds, the trip latch and its kind.

A threshold of 0 disables that protection. When the operating point crosses one the trip is
latched and the input stops conducting (the mode loop opens); :meth:`op_clear` resets it (the
model's protection-clear command). The thresholds are checked on
the solved operating point, so a trip is a DC behaviour, not a transient one. The latch, the
threshold judging and the trip/kind/clear replies are the shared protection primitive
(:class:`ProtectionLatch`); the load adds no increment of its own — while the latch stands,
the input stage simply does not conduct.

``ocp_enabled`` / ``opp_enabled`` switch those protections, and ``ocp_delay`` /
``opp_delay`` let the over-limit stand that long (virtual time) before the trip — the latch
falls when the limit is still exceeded at the deadline (the B&K 8600 CURR:PROT:DEL). Its
status flags are the 8600's questionable bits: OV and VF while OVP stands, OC while the
current is over its limit or OCP stands, OP likewise for power, PS while OCP or OPP stands.

file_system.label: 文件系统
file_system.about: 仪表的驱动器、文件夹和文件，存放在工程师的电脑上。
file_system.about_en: The instrument's drives, folders and files, kept on the engineer's computer.
file_system.doc:
An instrument's drives, folders and files (MMEMory, :DISK), on the engineer's computer.

``drives`` lists the drive words the instrument knows (``INTernal`` answers to ``INT:`` and
``INTERNAL:``; the first is the default drive); ``home`` is the current folder after power-on
(and after ``*RST`` when ``reset_home``); it exists from the start. Errors are the definition's
codes: ``name_error`` for a refused path (escape, forbidden character, symbolic link, a folder
not empty), ``not_found`` for a missing file, folder or drive, ``full`` for the capacity.
Catalogs: ``mmemory`` gives ``<used>,<free>{,"<name>,<type>,<size>"}`` (Keysight MMEMory);
``lines`` gives the count, then one name per line. Model limits: the drives are folders of the
engineer's computer, so the space a catalog reports is the files' bytes against ``capacity``,
not the instrument's own bookkeeping; no hidden or system files, no file locks.

function_generator_core.label: 波形发生
function_generator_core.about: 生成标准波形，改频率时相位连续。
function_generator_core.about_en: Standard waveforms with phase-continuous frequency changes.
function_generator_core.doc:
Standard waveforms with phase-continuous frequency changes.

Parameters: ``function`` (SINusoid, SQUare, RAMP, DC; Siglent's SINE, SQUARE are the same),
``frequency`` (Hz), ``amplitude`` (Vpp), ``offset`` (V), ``phase`` (degrees), ``duty`` (% high,
square), ``symmetry`` (% rising, ramp; 100 is a sawtooth), ``bandwidth`` (Hz, harmonic limit for
square and ramp), ``rolloff`` (``brickwall``: the edges ring, Gibbs; ``gaussian``: no overshoot,
a 10–90 % edge of about 0.34 / bandwidth), ``square_max`` (Hz, highest square/ramp frequency),
``amplitude_unit`` (what ``amplitude`` means: VPP, VPK or VRMS of the waveform).

input_port.label: 输入端口
input_port.about: 电气输入，对地呈电阻（可选并联电容）阻抗。
input_port.about_en: An electrical input with a resistive (and optional capacitive) impedance to ground.
input_port.doc: An electrical input with a resistive (and optional capacitive) impedance to ground.

lead.label: 测试导线
lead.about: 连在线上的测试导线：一段真实的串联电阻。
lead.about_en: A test lead on a wire: a real series resistance.
lead.doc:
A test lead on a wire: a real series resistance.

Unlike a ``series`` accessory such as a cable, it is not negligible: the termination check does
not look through it and the bench circuit solves the drop across it.

load_resistor.label: 对地电阻
load_resistor.about: 一端接到测试台地的电阻，作为单端网络的负载。
load_resistor.about_en: A resistor from its one terminal to the bench ground, a load on a single-ended net.
load_resistor.doc: A resistor from its one terminal to the bench ground (a load on a single-ended net).

lockin_aux.label: AUX 输入输出
lockin_aux.about: 锁相放大器的四路辅助 ADC 输入和四路 DAC 输出。
lockin_aux.about_en: The lock-in's four auxiliary ADC inputs and four DAC outputs.
lockin_aux.doc:
The AUX block: four ADC inputs and four DAC outputs on the bench, circuit level.

Each input is a high-impedance (``z_in`` to ground) ADC terminal; each output is a Thevenin
source of ``dac`` volts behind ``z_out``. The inputs read the solved voltage of their nets, so a
wire to another instrument or a DUT matters exactly as it does for any other circuit block.

lockin_input_amp.label: 输入放大
lockin_input_amp.about: 低噪声前置放大：灵敏度满量程、动态储备、输入极限和噪声密度。
lockin_input_amp.about_en: The low-noise front end: sensitivity, dynamic reserve, input limit and noise density.
lockin_input_amp.doc:
The low-noise front-end amplifier: the sensitivity full scale, the dynamic reserve,
the absolute input limit and the front-end noise density.

Readings are input-referred (the gain does not scale X, Y or R); sensitivity sets full scale for
the overload limits and the auto-gain ladder, and the reserve widens the limit over it. The
signal itself passes through unchanged, which is what makes the outputs input-referred.

lockin_input_filter.label: 输入滤波
lockin_input_filter.about_en: Input coupling and the line-frequency notches.
lockin_input_filter.doc:
The input coupling and the line-frequency notches (the SR830 block diagram).

AC coupling is a first-order high-pass at ``ac_corner``; the line notch (and its second
harmonic) is a second-order band-stop of quality ``notch_q`` at ``line_frequency``. Both act on
the spectral lines (data level, like the coupling the old monolith applied); the input
impedance, shielding and the differential pair are the circuit part of the input terminal.

lockin_input_mode.label: 输入方式
lockin_input_mode.about: 输入配置：单端 A、差分 A − B 或电流输入。
lockin_input_mode.about_en: The input configuration: single-ended A, differential A − B, or current.
lockin_input_mode.doc:
The input configuration (the SR830's ISRC): single-ended A, differential A − B, or the
current input.

The terminals are ``input_port`` blocks in front (their impedance is the circuit part: 10 MΩ
for the voltage inputs; the current input is ``current_z`` to a virtual ground, so the
definition binds the A port's ``z_in`` to the same setting). This block forms the signal the
chain measures: A, A − B, or the current into A (its voltage over ``current_z``) times
``current_scale`` V/A, so the voltage sensitivities read as currents scaled by 1/current_scale
(``lockin_output.unit_scale``). Shield grounding is not a circuit element here: bench nets
are referred to one ground, so floating or grounding the shield changes no reading.

lockin_lowpass.label: 低通滤波
lockin_lowpass.about: n 阶 RC 低通：时间常数、斜率、建立过程和等效噪声带宽。
lockin_lowpass.about_en: The n-pole RC low-pass: time constant, slope, settling and noise bandwidth.
lockin_lowpass.doc:
The n-pole RC low-pass: time constant, slope (6 dB/oct per pole), the closed-form
settling from a new regime, the equivalent noise bandwidth, and the truncation check that
queues 329 when a truncated input still passes the filter.

lockin_mixer.label: 相敏检波
lockin_mixer.about: 把输入的谱线与参考相乘，得到检测频率附近的分量。
lockin_mixer.about_en: Multiplies the input's spectral lines by the reference, near the detection frequency.
lockin_mixer.doc:
The phase-sensitive detector: the input's spectral lines multiplied by the
reference, each becoming a complex exponential at Δf = f − f_detect, plus the input's DC term.
The low-pass filter is applied to those exponentials by ``lockin_lowpass``.

lockin_output.label: 直流输出
lockin_output.about: X/Y 与 R/θ 输出，含偏置、扩展、过载标志和自动增益/相位。
lockin_output.about_en: X/Y and R/θ outputs, with offset, expansion, overload flags and auto gain/phase.
lockin_output.doc:
The DC output: X/Y with offset and expansion, R/θ, the overload flags and their
errors, the front-end noise of the reading, auto gain and auto phase — and the sampler the data
buffer reads (X/Y/R/θ at the buffer's instants).

Offset and expansion are display-level: ``offset_x``/``offset_y`` are percent of full scale
(subtracted) and ``expand`` multiplies the deviation from the offset; R and θ always show the
raw outputs. The defaults (0 %, x1) leave X and Y untouched.

lockin_reference.label: 参考源
lockin_reference.about: 内部振荡器或跟踪 REF_IN 的基波；谐波次数；SINE_OUT 输出。
lockin_reference.about_en: Internal oscillator or tracking of REF_IN; harmonic n; the SINE_OUT drive.
lockin_reference.doc:
Internal oscillator or tracking of the fundamental on REF_IN; harmonic n; SINE_OUT drive.

Outputs: ``ref``, a unit line at the detection frequency n·f whose phase is n·ψ + φ (the
demodulator's reference), and ``sine``, the SINE_OUT drive at f (``amplitude`` in V rms) on
the dc ``dc_level``.
An external reference needs at least ``min_vpp`` peak to peak; when it disappears the
oscillator keeps running at the last frequency and error 327 is queued once.

mux_card.label: 多路复用卡
mux_card.about: 多路复用卡的继电器和模拟总线。
mux_card.about_en: A multiplexer card's relays and analog bus.
mux_card.doc:
A multiplexer card's relays and analog bus (34901A, 20 channels).

Every channel is a two-wire input (``H``/``L``); a closed relay connects it to the card's
internal analog bus through the contact resistance ``relay_r``. The bus carries the internal
DMM's input resistance (asked of the ``dmm`` terminal, so a high-impedance range changes it)
and its voltage is the signal the internal DMM measures — closing a channel therefore loads
the DUT on that channel. ``close_limit`` is the number of relays that may be closed at once:
the card is break-before-make while scanning, so the default is one, and a second
closure is refused (-221).

The relay state lives in the instrument's channel state (``ch<n>.<relay_state>``, declared as
``channel_state`` by the definition); the card reads it whenever it stamps the circuit.

optical_attenuator.label: 光衰减器
optical_attenuator.about: 光纤上的固定光衰减器：与频率无关的固定损耗（dB）。
optical_attenuator.about_en: A fixed optical attenuator on a fibre: a flat loss in dB.
optical_attenuator.doc: A fixed optical attenuator on a fibre: ``attenuation`` dB of loss, flat in frequency.

optical_power_meter.label: 光功率计
optical_power_meter.about: 光功率计的探头与测量：平均光功率，按所设波长校准。
optical_power_meter.about_en: An optical power meter's head and measurement: average power, calibrated at the set wavelength.
optical_power_meter.doc:
An optical power meter's detector head and its measurement: the average optical
power on ``in``, read in W, dBm or dB against a reference, with the calibration of the
wavelength it is set to.

The detector's spectral response (``spectral_response``, relative responsivity against
wavelength) is calibrated out at the set ``wavelength``: light of another wavelength reads
off by R(λ actual)/R(λ set), as on a real meter told the wrong wavelength. ``offset_w`` is the
dark offset until ``zero`` takes it out (zeroing with light on the detector takes that light
too, as on the real one). Ranges (``ranges``, the top of each in dBm) are picked automatically
or set; light above the range in use reads ``over_value``. Reading noise uses the meter
``noise`` parameter on the range's full scale in W at the ``averaging_time``; ``calibration_error``
is the gain error in dB.

It is a ``TraceSource`` (``POWer`` in W, ``DBM``): a ``curve_buffer`` logs it at a rate or per
trigger, each point at its own instant — during a laser sweep each point sees the wavelength of
its instant.

optical_receiver.label: 光接收机
optical_receiver.about: 光电探测器与放大器：把光功率转换成电压，带宽受限。
optical_receiver.about_en: A photodetector and its amplifier: optical power becomes volts, band-limited.
optical_receiver.doc:
A photodetector and its amplifier: optical power on ``in`` (W) becomes volts on ``out``,
v = P · ``responsivity`` (A/W) · ``transimpedance`` (V/A), band-limited by ``response`` at
``bandwidth``. A calibrated optical channel (a sampling head that shows watts) sets the
transimpedance to 1/responsivity: one volt per watt.

``noise_w`` is the input-referred optical noise (W rms over the receiver's bandwidth, as data
sheets give it); the record taker adds it with the sampler's own (``output_noise_rms``), since
an analytic signal carries no noise. Average power (``power``) is the mean
of the light arriving, as a power meter in the receiver's DC path reads it.

optical_source.label: 光源
optical_source.about: 激光器与调制器：电驱动决定输出光功率。
optical_source.about_en: A laser and its modulator: the electrical drive sets the optical power.
optical_source.doc:
A laser and its modulator: the electrical drive on ``in`` sets the optical power on ``out``.

Linear around the operating point: the drive's DC is the bias, and a drive of ±``swing``/2
about it swings the power between the zero and one levels that ``power`` (average) and
``extinction_ratio`` give — P(t) = Pavg + OMA/2 · (v(t) − v_dc)/(swing/2), OMA = P1 − P0. A
drive beyond ±swing/2 is not clipped (the modulator is linear here, a model limit): keep the
drive inside the swing, as a real driver is set up. Off (``enabled`` false): no light.

output_control_loop.label: CV/CC 控制环
output_control_loop.about: 电压/电流控制环及其限流切换，可供任何输出级复用。
output_control_loop.about_en: The voltage/current control loop and its limit switch, reusable by any output stage.
output_control_loop.doc:
The voltage/current control loop and its limit switch, reusable by any output stage.

A definition binds the setpoint (``function``, ``v_level``, ``i_level``), the limits
(``i_limit``, ``v_limit``) and the output setting to it. The piecewise output stage calls
:meth:`update_mode` with the metered terminal voltage and the source current; the loop picks
CV or CC and the sign of a current-limited source, as the SMU's output stage does.

``envelope`` optionally names a component whose ``limit_cap(function, level)`` caps a limit by
the range in use (the SMU's source DAC); a supply that has no such table leaves it empty. A
channel-level loop names its channel's ``power_stage`` in ``channel_envelope`` instead.

output_stage.label: 输出级
output_stage.about: 由信号输入驱动电气引脚的戴维南源。
output_stage.about_en: A Thevenin source driving an electrical pin from a signal input.
output_stage.doc:
A Thevenin source driving an electrical pin from a signal input.

``load_setting`` is the load the instrument assumes when it defines its amplitude: the
source EMF is scaled so that a load of that value would see the requested voltage. ``inf`` means
the amplitude is the open-circuit voltage; so does any setting of ``hiz_from`` ohms or more, for
instruments whose high-impedance setting is a number (a calibrator's ``LOAD 10000``).

passive_probe.label: 无源探头
passive_probe.about: 分压探头：从探针（IN）到示波器接头（OUT）的串联电阻。
passive_probe.about_en: A divider probe: series resistance from the tip (IN) to the scope connector (OUT).
passive_probe.doc:
A divider probe: series resistance from tip (IN) to the scope connector (OUT).

With ``attenuation`` N and ``r_tip`` the total tip resistance into the nominal scope input
``r_scope`` (1 MΩ), the series element is ``r_tip - r_scope`` (9 MΩ for a 10x, 10 MΩ probe).
The division then follows from the scope's actual input impedance, as on a real bench.
Probe capacitance and compensation are not modeled (transients are out of scope).

power_output.label: 电源输出级
power_output.about: 电源通道的输出继电器、远端采样和控制环驱动的源。
power_output.about_en: A supply channel's output relay, remote sense and the source the loop programs.
power_output.doc:
The output stage: relay, remote sense and the source the loop programs.

The relay closes ``relay_s`` after the output is switched on (and opens at once when it is
switched off), so the output timings count in virtual time. The source is a voltage
source regulating the sense pair (or the force terminals) in CV mode, a current source in CC
mode — the same elements the SMU's output stage uses, driven by the reused control loop.

power_stage.label: 电源功率级
power_stage.about: 电源通道的电压/电流能力和限流上限。
power_stage.about_en: A supply channel's voltage/current capability and current-limit cap.
power_stage.doc:
The channel's power stage: voltage/current capability and the current-limit cap.

``limit_cap`` is what the reused ``output_control_loop`` asks its envelope: the current limit a
channel may program. ``v_max`` is the voltage ceiling the output stage clips the programmed
level to, so a definition whose state allows a wider number still cannot over-drive the stage.

power_supply_setpoint.label: 电源设定 DAC
power_supply_setpoint.about: 电源通道的电压和电流设定，限在通道的量程内。
power_supply_setpoint.about_en: A supply channel's voltage and current levels, within its range.
power_supply_setpoint.doc:
A channel's setpoint DAC: the voltage and current levels, within the channel's
range (``stage.v_max`` / ``stage.i_max``). The control loop programs from the same settings.

prbs_source.label: PRBS 码型
prbs_source.about: 按符号率输出的伪随机码型，NRZ 或 PAM4。
prbs_source.about_en: A pseudo-random pattern at the symbol rate, NRZ or PAM4.
prbs_source.doc:
A pseudo-random pattern at ``rate`` symbols/s between ±``level``: NRZ (one bit per symbol)
or PAM4 (two bits per symbol, four levels, Gray coded: :func:`pam4_symbols`).

Periodic with 2^n − 1 symbols, so its spectrum is lines at k·rate/N: the DFT of the sequence
times the rectangular pulse's sinc. Exact, not estimated by an FFT of samples; lines are
kept for ``lobes`` sinc lobes, within the line limit. Symbol 0 starts at time zero (the
pattern's start, which a sampling scope's pattern lock finds).

rc_lowpass.label: RC 低通
rc_lowpass.about: IN 到 OUT 串联电阻、OUT 对地电容的低通滤波器。
rc_lowpass.about_en: Series R from IN to OUT and C from OUT to ground.
rc_lowpass.doc: Series R from IN to OUT, C from OUT to ground. ``tol_r`` / ``tol_c`` are hidden tolerances.

reading_buffer.label: 读数缓冲区
reading_buffer.about: 具名的读数存储：万用表的读数存储、SMU 的 defbuffer1 等。
reading_buffer.about_en: Named reading buffers: a DMM's reading memory, an SMU's defbuffer1 and others.
reading_buffer.doc:
Named reading buffers: a DMM's reading memory, an SMU's ``defbuffer1`` and the ones a script
makes. Commands name a buffer with ``name``; without one they use ``default``.

reading_math.label: 读数运算
reading_math.about: A/D 之后的运算：平均、mx+b、百分比/dB/dBm、限值和统计。
reading_math.about_en: A meter's math after the A/D: average, mx+b, percent/dB/dBm, limits and statistics.
reading_math.doc:
A meter's math after the A/D: average, (m·x − c)/z, percent/dB/dBm, limits and statistics.

A sampler between the meter's A/D (``source``) and its trigger model; ``measure`` replaces the
A/D's for the measurement commands. Model limits: the statistics are those of the readings that
passed through since they were cleared, not a recomputation over the reading memory.

reference_clock.label: 参考时钟
reference_clock.about: 源的频率参考：有偏差的内部振荡器，或外接 10 MHz。
reference_clock.about_en: The source's frequency reference: an internal oscillator with its error, or an external 10 MHz.
reference_clock.doc:
The source's frequency reference: an internal oscillator off by ``ppm`` (hidden; a deviations
entry), or with ``source`` EXTernal the 10 MHz on ``ref`` when one within ±10 ppm is there (the
internal oscillator otherwise, as a real source falls back when it cannot lock).

resistor.label: 电阻
resistor.about_en: A resistor between terminals A and B.
resistor.doc: A resistor between its two terminals A and B.

rf_attenuator.label: 输出衰减器
rf_attenuator.about: 射频源的输出步进衰减器。
rf_attenuator.about_en: The RF source's output step attenuator.
rf_attenuator.doc:
The output step attenuator. This model has no attenuation steps — its level is
exact over the whole range — so ``attenuation`` is 0 dB unless a
definition sets it.

rf_level_control.label: 电平控制（ALC）
rf_level_control.about: 射频输出电平控制：把 50 Ω 负载上的 dBm 换算成载波电动势。
rf_level_control.about_en: The RF level control: dBm into 50 Ω converted to the carrier's EMF.
rf_level_control.doc:
The level control and ALC: the level in dBm into a matched 50 Ω load. The model's
level is exact over the whole range (no ALC dynamics, settling or level error), so this block is the conversion from dBm to the carrier's EMF.

rf_mod_source.label: 调制源
rf_mod_source.about: 内部低频调制源：AM、FM 或 PM 的调制音。
rf_mod_source.about_en: The internal low-frequency source: the tone of AM, FM or PM.
rf_mod_source.doc:
The internal low-frequency modulation source: the tone of AM, FM or PM at its set
frequency. Its frequency is synthesized from the same timebase as the carrier, so the
reference's error scales it too; FM modulates with a phase shift of −π/2 (a sine tone), PM in
phase with the carrier.

rf_modulator.label: 调制器
rf_modulator.about: 把 AM、FM/PM 调制加到载波上。
rf_modulator.about_en: Applies AM and FM/PM modulation to the carrier.
rf_modulator.doc:
The modulator: AM, and Bessel FM/PM truncated at Carson's rule, applied to the
carrier line. FM and PM are exclusive (the later one wins with -221), AM may be added to
either, pulse modulation is refused (-221), and a modulation index needing more than
``LINE_BUDGET`` lines is refused (-222) on the setting that causes it. ``enabled`` is the
master switch: off, the carrier passes bare and every modulation keeps its settings.

rf_reference.label: 10 MHz 参考
rf_reference.about: 射频源的 10 MHz 时基及 REF_OUT 输出。
rf_reference.about_en: The RF source's 10 MHz timebase and the REF_OUT output.
rf_reference.doc:
The 10 MHz timebase: the generic reference clock, plus the REF_OUT output.

``ppm`` is the timebase error: hidden state, readable only by measuring. With ``source``
EXTernal the 10 MHz on ``ref`` locks the generator when one within ±10 ppm is there, and every
synthesized frequency carries that error instead; REF_OUT carries the error of the timebase in
use (10 MHz at +4 dBm into a matched load).

rf_synthesizer.label: 载波合成
rf_synthesizer.about: 载波频率合成：连续波，或扫描/列表及其当前点。
rf_synthesizer.about_en: The carrier synthesizer: CW frequency, or the sweep/list plan and its current point.
rf_synthesizer.doc:
The carrier synthesizer: the CW frequency, or the sweep/list plan and its current
point, advanced by ``:INITiate`` and ``:TRIGger``. The line it emits is unit amplitude at the
set frequency times the timebase error of the reference it locks to; level and modulation come
later in the chain.

sampling_acquisition.label: 等效时间采集
sampling_acquisition.about: 等效时间采样示波器带码型锁定的采集。
sampling_acquisition.about_en: The acquisition of an equivalent-time sampling scope with pattern lock.
sampling_acquisition.doc:
The acquisition of an equivalent-time sampling scope with pattern lock.

Trigger: the ``clock`` (a ``clock_recovery``) locked to the data; with ``pattern_lock`` the
record's time zero is the pattern's start and the record repeats with the pattern. The record
spans ``divs`` divisions of ``scale`` from ``position`` (s after the pattern start) in
``points`` samples; each sample is the channel's signal (wired to ``in<n>``, after its
``vertical``, a ``scope_vertical`` giving scale, offset and the sampler's noise per division)
at its instant plus the timebase jitter (``jitter_s`` rms), plus the noise of the vertical and
of the channel components named in ``noise_from`` (their ``output_noise_rms``, e.g. an
``optical_receiver``), added in power. ``averages`` (while ``average``) records are averaged:
noise falls by √N, jitter is averaged into the shape as a real scope's average does.

An acquisition takes ``points × averages / sample_rate`` of virtual time (the sampler takes
``sample_rate`` samples per second) plus ``overhead_s``. Not locked, or without pattern lock
(eye mode, not modelled), it is refused with ``unlocked_error``. ``adc`` (optional) quantizes.

The surface a scope's measurements, waveform transfer and screen read is the real-time
acquisition's: ``read_record``, ``transfer_record``, ``measure_record``, ``displayed``,
``compute``, ``records``, ``acq_count``.

scan_table.label: 扫描表
scan_table.about: 作为一次运行读取的通道列表，及其背后的采样器。
scan_table.about_en: A channel list read as one run, and the sampler behind it.
scan_table.doc:
The scan table: a channel list read as one run, and the sampler behind it.

``list`` is the scan list in SCPI channel numbers (a definition binds it to an ``int_list``
setting, e.g. ``ROUT:SCAN (@101:110)``); ``ascending`` scans it in ascending channel order (the
34970A's rule) instead of the order it was written; ``count`` is how many times the list is
scanned per run and ``interval`` the wait between two scans (stored for the model's timing;
each reading takes the relay settling time plus the DMM's reading time).
The scan runs
through the trigger model: each of its readings closes its channel (the card's
break-before-make rule), reads the internal DMM and carries the channel number in the ``CHAN``
field, so the reading buffer keeps channel and value together.

scope_acquisition.label: 采集
scope_acquisition.about: 示波器的运行控制、采样和记录。
scope_acquisition.about_en: A scope's run control, sampling and records.
scope_acquisition.doc:
Run control, sampling and the records of a scope, built from the scope's modules.

One component for every oscilloscope model, set by parameters.
It names the modules it reads: ``horizontal`` (a ``scope_timebase``), ``trigger`` (a
``scope_trigger``), ``adc`` (a ``scope_adc``), and per channel ``vertical`` (a
``scope_vertical``: the scale and offset) and ``probe`` (a ``scope_probe``, whose output is wired
to ``in<n>``). Written the earlier way, with the modules' parameters on the acquisition itself and
no module named, the definition is expanded into the modules when it loads (a macro):

* **run control** ``mode`` and the values that mean ``auto``, ``normal``, ``single``, ``stop``
  and ``force`` (one frame whatever the trigger, then stop); ``after_single`` is the mode a
  completed single acquisition leaves (empty: the mode stays and the scope stops).
  ``reacquire`` says when a read gets a new acquisition from a running scope: ``explicit``
  (only a digitize command), ``every_read`` or ``on_read_start`` (a read from the first point;
  later pieces read the same record). A pending single acquisition is retried on every read.
  ``missing: acquire`` reads a channel that has no record yet, ``error`` refuses it;
* **noise** the input noise comes from the channel's ``scope_vertical`` ``noise_table``, per
  division at the input connector, in display volts times the probe ratio; it is keyed by
  ``noise_key``: ``time`` (the absolute sample instants; ``noise_stream`` names a setting
  that selects another stream) or ``acquisition`` (the acquisition count, so pauses of any
  real length between commands give the same numbers); ``trigger_jitter_s``;
  * **processing** what the quantized codes go through: ``normal`` keeps them;
    ``average`` (``averages``) is the mean of that many acquisitions, each of them noisy and
    quantized, so the noise falls by √N and the resolution gains (it takes N acquisitions'
    time); ``peak`` examines each record interval at the ADC's native rate (at most
    ``peak_max_oversample`` samples per record sample) and keeps, of the interval's smallest
    and largest code, the one that departs farther from its ends — a pulse the record rate
    would step over shows up; ``eres`` smooths ``4**eres_bits`` codes (a boxcar), so the
    noise falls by ``2**eres_bits`` — that many more effective bits, at the boxcar's
    bandwidth.

* **synchronization**: ``completion: immediate`` finishes a
  single acquisition, a digitize or a forced frame within the command that starts it;
  ``pending`` makes it an operation that finishes in virtual time, when the record after the
  trigger is full: until then the trigger status is waiting (then triggered), a read gets the
  previous record (``while_waiting: previous``) or an error (``error``), ``*OPC?`` and ``*WAI``
  wait for it unless ``opc_waits`` is false, and a digitize waits for it. Without a trigger it
  waits for one, looking again whenever a command arrives; ``no_trigger: wait`` leaves ``*OPC?``
  unanswered meanwhile (the client times out), ``return`` answers it at once.

* **segmented memory**: with ``segments`` above one (while ``segmented``), a single
  acquisition or a digitize takes that many records, each on its own trigger; the trigger is
  armed for the next ``rearm_s`` after a record is full, and the acquisition is done with its
  last segment (in an auto mode a segment whose trigger does not come within the auto timeout
  is taken untriggered; otherwise the acquisition waits). ``segment_index`` (from 1) selects
  the segment that reads, transfers and measurements use; op ``figure`` gives the number of
  segments acquired and the selected segment's time tag. ``memory_points`` limits segments
  times record length (-221). The first segment's noise is an unsegmented acquisition's; each
  later one has its own.

Status events (for ``status_register`` bits of these names): ``TRG`` when a stored acquisition met
its trigger, ``DONE`` for every stored acquisition, ``AUTO`` for one an auto mode took without
its trigger, ``ARM`` when a run or a single acquisition arms the trigger.

Per-channel ``ch<n>.display`` says which channels are acquired. The trigger status
(``status_text``), an acquisition type with its count (``acquire_type``, ``acquire_counts``)
and the read-only figures (op ``figure``: points, sample rate, acquisitions) are declared.
Measurements are a ``scope_measurements`` module, the transfer and its preamble a
``waveform_transfer``.

scope_adc.label: ADC 组
scope_adc.about: 各通道共用的 ADC：分辨率、最高采样率和交织。
scope_adc.about_en: The ADC group the channels share: resolution, top sample rates and interleaving.
scope_adc.doc:
The ADC group shared by a scope's channels: where each channel's analog signal becomes
samples, its resolution, top sample rates and interleaving.

``in<n>`` takes channel n's signal in display volts (the probe module's output); ``out<n>``
gives its sample stream. A frame is made in this order: the signal is evaluated at the
request's instants, less the channel's skew (a digital delay; ``probe``); the input noise of
the channel's vertical division (``vertical``) is added, drawn from the request's random
stream; the sum is quantized. The samples are the codes, kept in volts — the format says
how many bits and what one code step is worth.

``bits`` (0: records are not quantized) and ``codes_per_div`` (0: ``2**bits / divs``) set the
quantization; ``offset_sign`` says whether the offset setting is added to or subtracted from the
volts. ``max_rate`` is the top sample rate (0: no limit); channels of a ``rate_pairs`` pair share
a converter, so with both on the top rate is ``max_rate_paired``.

``min_full_scale`` (V at the input; 0: none) is the hardware's smallest range: a division
smaller than ``min_full_scale / divs`` magnifies that range, so the code step stays the range's
(a ``codes_per_div``-th of ``min_full_scale / divs``) and the converter clips at the range's
edges, not the screen's.

The converter's own non-idealities, referred to a sine that spans the converter's range
(0 dBFS): ``distortion_table`` rows ``[V/div at the input, HD2 dBc, HD3 dBc]`` (the row of the
largest division not above the setting) bend the signal around the middle of the range with
x² and x³ terms — a smaller signal has less, HD2 falling 6 dB and HD3 12 dB per halving, as a
polynomial's do. A row may also name the input frequency it holds at, ``[V/div, Hz, HD2, HD3]``:
the rows of one division are interpolated linearly over frequency (outside them the
nearest holds) at the frequency of the signal's strongest line. ``enob_table`` rows ``[Hz, ENOB]`` give the
effective bits of a full-scale sine at that frequency (interpolated the same way): the converter
adds the noise that brings the record down to them — what the input noise, the quantization,
the distortion and the aperture jitter leave of the error budget; none when they already exceed
it. An input without a line gets the lowest frequency's noise: the floor stays. ``interleave`` sub-converters on the ``max_rate`` grid differ by one cosine
pattern in gain (``interleave_image_dbc``: each image at k·fs/N ± f) and offset
(``interleave_spur_dbfs``: the spur at k·fs/N), and each sub-converter may carry its own gain
error, offset and sampling-time skew (``interleave_gain_errors``, ``interleave_offsets_fs``,
``interleave_skews_s``, one value per sub-converter) — the images and spurs are then the
discrete Fourier series of those lists. A record slower than ``max_rate`` takes every M-th of the
full-rate samples, so its samples keep their sub-converters and the pattern folds into its band
(every N-th: one sub-converter, a gain error and a DC offset); ``aperture_jitter_s`` moves each sample instant
by its own draw (σ rms), whose noise on a sine of frequency f is 2πf·σ of it. Unset (the
defaults), none is drawn and the frames are what they were.

scope_attenuator.label: 输入衰减器
scope_attenuator.about: 通道输入端的步进衰减器：按输入 V/div 选一档衰减，前置放大器把增益补回。
scope_attenuator.about_en: The channel's input step attenuator: a loss per input V/div range, made up by the preamplifier.
scope_attenuator.doc:
The channel's input step attenuator: one loss per range of input V/div (``steps``, rows of
[up to V/div, loss dB], the first row whose V/div is not below the setting). The preamplifier
after it (a ``scope_vertical`` naming it as its ``attenuator``) restores the gain, so the
record is unchanged; what the attenuator decides is the level the preamplifier sees, which an
internal probe on its output shows. The input V/div is the displayed ``scale`` over the
``probe_ratio`` the display includes, as the vertical takes it.

scope_autoscale.label: 自动设置
scope_autoscale.about: 示波器的自动设置（前面板 Autoscale 键，:AUToscale）。
scope_autoscale.doc:
The autoscale of an oscilloscope (the front panel's Autoscale key, :AUToscale).

Each channel searched is acquired at its coarsest scale, then again at the scale and offset its
record asks for, until they settle (``passes``): the waveform's spread is read between the
0.05 and 99.95 percentiles, so the scale puts it over ``fill_divs`` divisions (the next value
of the 1-2-5 sequence), the offset centres it. A waveform is there when the record's spread
beyond the channel's noise (its ``scope_vertical`` noise table at that scale) exceeds
``presence`` noise rms, or its mean is beyond ``dc_floor``; it is triggerable when it swings
through a band of ``presence`` noise rms around its middle (a DC level is not). ``STACk``
gives each waveform its own band of the screen, ``OVERlay`` and ``SEParate`` (each grid the
whole range) the full screen.

The timebase shows ``periods`` periods of the lowest-numbered channel's waveform. The period is
its fundamental, the lowest of its spectral lines above a twentieth of the strongest — as the
trigger's counter sees it, without the noise: a SimuBench simplification of the scope's
search (a waveform without lines, a DC level, keeps the timebase). The edge trigger takes the
first triggerable channel in ``trigger_order``, its level the waveform's middle; ``writes``
are the settings autoscale leaves at fixed values (the trigger mode, slope and sweep, the marker
mode, the functions off). Nothing found: every setting as it was.

scope_decimator.label: 抽取与采集方式
scope_decimator.about: 从 ADC 采样率降到记录采样率：各采集方式。
scope_decimator.about_en: From the ADC's rate to the record's: the acquisition modes.
scope_decimator.doc:
From the ADC's rate to the record's: the acquisition modes.

``in<n>`` takes channel n's samples at the converter's rate, ``out<n>`` gives them at the
record's rate, after ``processing``:

* ``normal`` keeps them;
* ``average`` (``averages``) is the mean of that many acquisitions, each of them noisy and
  quantized, so the noise falls by √N and the resolution gains (it takes N acquisitions' time);
* ``peak`` examines each record interval at the ADC's native rate (at most
  ``peak_max_oversample`` samples per record sample) and keeps, of the interval's smallest and
  largest code, the one that departs farther from its ends — a pulse the record rate would step
  over shows up;
* ``eres`` smooths ``4**eres_bits`` codes (a boxcar), so the noise falls by ``2**eres_bits`` —
  that many more effective bits, at the boxcar's bandwidth.

A request's ``index0`` is counted on the converter's grid (:meth:`oversample` samples per record
sample): the k-th acquisition of an average continues the random stream after the previous
one's samples there.

scope_dsp_filter.label: 数字带宽滤波
scope_dsp_filter.about: ADC 之后的数字低通：砖墙、高斯、Bessel 或 Butterworth 形，关时直通。
scope_dsp_filter.about_en: A digital low-pass after the ADC: brick wall, Gaussian, Bessel or Butterworth; off: a pass-through.
scope_dsp_filter.doc:
A digital low-pass on each channel's samples, between the ADC and the decimator.

``in<n>`` takes channel n's samples (the converter's, or an earlier filter's), ``out<n>`` gives
them filtered: a zero-phase ``response`` (``brickwall``: flat magnitude, linear phase with the
delay removed — ringing on a step; ``gaussian``; ``bessel4``; ``butterworth4``) with -3 dB at
``bandwidth`` (-6 dB for the brick wall's edge), while ``enabled``. Off, or at a ``bandwidth`` of
``passthrough_hz`` or more (the analog bandwidth already limits the signal), the samples pass
unchanged, bit for bit. Each parameter may name a channel's own setting (``$ch{n}.isim_type``).

The filter is a FIR kernel (the shape's impulse response, a Blackman window, unit gain at
0 Hz) reaching 32 periods of the cutoff on either side, at most 32768 converter samples: a frame
asks its upstream for that much more on either side and keeps the middle (no history
is kept). A record slower than the converter (``adc``'s top rate) is filtered at up
to ``max_oversample`` times its own rate and then decimated — the hardware filters at the
converter's rate, so the noise above the record's Nyquist frequency is filtered too.
Limits: the window widens the brick wall's edge to about a fifth of the cutoff (stop band
below -70 dB); a cutoff so far below the rate that the reach is cut at 32768 samples gets a
wider edge in proportion; below the converter's rate by more than ``max_oversample`` the
noise between the record's Nyquist frequency and the analog bandwidth is not filtered.

scope_frontend.label: 模拟前端（旧名）
scope_frontend.about: 垂直通道的旧名称，行为相同，保留以载入旧定义。
scope_frontend.about_en: The earlier name of the vertical channel, kept so existing definitions load.
scope_frontend.doc: The earlier name of ``scope_vertical`` (same behavior), kept so existing definitions load.

scope_math.label: 数学运算
scope_math.about: 示波器的数学函数：运算、变换以及对其迹线的测量。
scope_math.about_en: A scope's math functions: operators, transforms and measurements on their traces.
scope_math.doc:
A scope's math functions (``FUNCtion1..N``): the operators, the transforms and the
measurements over their traces, computed from the acquisition's records when they are read.

Each function's definition lives in the settings under ``prefix`` + its number —
``function1.operator``, ``function1.source1``, ``function1.display``, ``function1.range``, …
— declared by the definition; the block reads them by path, so one block serves every
function a model has. A source names a channel, another function (a cycle is -221) or a
constant. Model limits: a transform longer than ``fft_max_points`` points or a span beyond
``fft_span_max`` is refused (-221/-222), never truncated; an unknown operand is -224.

scope_measurements.label: 自动测量
scope_measurements.about: 对示波器记录做自动测量。
scope_measurements.about_en: Automatic measurements on a scope's records.

scope_probe.label: 探头设置
scope_probe.about: 通道的探头衰减比：显示电压等于输入电压乘以衰减比。
scope_probe.about_en: A channel's probe ratio: display volts are input volts times the ratio.
scope_probe.doc:
The probe setting of one channel: display volts are the volts at the input times ``ratio``.

A display conversion, not part of the analog path. ``skew``
(bound to the model's channel-skew setting where it has one) and ``skew_error`` (this unit's
own, a ``deviations`` draw) delay the channel's record by that many seconds: the acquisition
samples the channel's signal that much earlier. A real
scope applies the delay after the ADC, so the trigger path — which detects on the analog
signal — is not delayed with it.

scope_sampler.label: 采样器
scope_sampler.about: 通道的采样保持：主采样器按最高采样率取样，再轮流分给几路较慢的采样器；各路的增益、偏置、时延失配与本通道的孔径抖动在采样时刻起作用。
scope_sampler.about_en: The channel's track-and-hold: a primary sampler at the top rate hands its samples in turn to slower path samplers; their gain, offset and timing mismatch and the channel's own aperture jitter act at the sample instants.
scope_sampler.doc:
The channel's track-and-hold sampler: a primary sampler at the converter's top rate that
hands its samples, in turn, to ``paths`` slower samplers, each feeding a group of the
converter's lanes. In track mode its output is its input (the analog path is unchanged); its
errors act at the sample instants, where the converter (a ``scope_adc`` naming it as its
``sampler``) applies them: each path's gain error, offset (fraction of the full scale) and
timing skew (s) repeat every ``paths`` samples of the top-rate grid, and
``aperture_jitter_s`` is this channel's own jitter, drawn per sample and per channel (the
clock all channels share is the timebase's ``clock_jitter_s``).

scope_timebase.label: 时基
scope_timebase.about: 水平系统：每格时间、记录长度规则和触发位置。
scope_timebase.about_en: The horizontal system: time per division, record length and trigger position.
scope_timebase.doc:
The horizontal system: time per division, the record length rule and the trigger position.

``record_length``: ``fixed`` (``points`` over ten divisions), ``exact`` (the rate is
``points / 10 div`` up to the ADC group's top rate), ``rate_ladder`` (that rate rounded down
to a 1-2-5 step; samples ``1 / rate`` apart) or ``rate_pow2`` (rounded down to the top rate
divided by a power of two, the Infiniium UXR's rates). A ``sample_rate`` above 0 sets the
rate instead of the points (a manual rate takes precedence over the memory depth, the
Infiniium guide's :ACQuire:SRATe): rounded up to the next rate of the rule's steps, at most the
top rate and at most ``max_points / 10 div``; the record then holds ``rate x 10 div`` points.
``max_points`` (the memory the unit has) also caps a set memory depth. The trigger sits at the centre, or ``delay``
seconds before it when that is bound. A model with a reference mode setting places it from
``reference_mode`` (DELay / POSition) and, in POSition mode, from ``reference_position``
percent across the record.

The sampling clock (the oscillator all channels share) has a jitter ``clock_jitter_s`` (white; ``clock_tie_s`` adds the slow phase drift, #1698) and a frequency error ``clock_ppm`` (this unit's own, a ``deviations``
draw); with ``rosc`` EXTernal it follows the 10 MHz on ``ref`` instead, whose fractional
error the instrument inherits. A fast clock takes samples
closer together than the nominal interval, so the records keep the nominal dt the scope
reports and time measurements read low — the spectrum analyzer's reference convention.

scope_trigger.label: 触发
scope_trigger.about: 在独立模拟通路上的边沿触发和脉宽（毛刺）触发。
scope_trigger.about_en: Edge and pulse-width (glitch) trigger on its own analog path.
scope_trigger.doc:
Edge and pulse-width (glitch) trigger on its own analog path.

The trigger looks at the signal before the ADC, through its own ``coupling`` filter (a table
``filters`` of high-pass and low-pass corners per coupling value: AC, low- and high-frequency
reject), a ``reject`` filter alongside it and ``hf_reject`` (filters keyed HF), with its own
``noise_rms``. An edge counts once the signal has been beyond the
``hysteresis_divs`` band on the far side of the level (``reject_hysteresis_divs`` while
``noise_reject`` is on); the instant is interpolated between samples, so a record reports the
trigger to a fraction of a sample. After a trigger, the next is not taken before ``holdoff``
seconds (while ``holdoff_on``).

``source``, ``level`` and ``slope`` select the edge (``rising`` and ``falling`` list the slope
names that take each); a level or slope per channel is bound with the channel number written
``{n}``: ``$ch{n}.trigger_level``. ``external`` sources read the ``ext`` port (wired from an
instrument input); ``line`` sources trigger on the rising zero crossings of the mains
(``line_hz``, phase zero at the session's start). An auto mode looks ``search_windows``
records ahead on the record's grid and on as far as ``auto_timeout_s`` of virtual time beyond
(its auto timeout: a signal that repeats within it triggers at any timebase); one that
finds nothing still takes only ``search_windows`` records. A normal or single acquisition
waits up to ``search_horizon_s`` of virtual time for its edge. Beyond the record's grid the
search takes a coarser one, and an edge found there is bisected on the signal (without the
trigger's noise) to a thousandth of a record sample.

``mode`` ``glitch`` triggers on a pulse by its width instead: a pulse
of ``polarity`` runs from one crossing of the level to the next opposite one — the same
interpolated crossings, hysteresis, coupling, noise and holdoff as the edge trigger — and
``qualifier`` compares that time with ``width_low`` and ``width_high``: ``less`` (narrower
than ``width_high``), ``range`` (between the two) and ``outside`` (narrower than ``width_low``
or wider than ``width_high``) trigger at the edge that ends the pulse; ``greater`` (wider than
``width_low``) triggers at the instant the pulse has lasted ``width_low`` (it need not have
ended), or with ``greater_at: end`` at the edge that ends it. The
whole pulse lies after the trigger is armed: one that began within the pre-trigger time or the
holdoff does not count. ``slope`` plays no part. The search takes the record grid for as many
samples as ``max_search_points`` allows (fewer for a signal of many lines), then a grid an
eighth of the narrowest width bound the qualifier uses for as many again, the instants there
bisected on the signal (without trigger noise); a pulse narrower than that grid can be missed
there, and an acquisition that finds nothing within that reach waits, looking again at the
next command.

The advanced families keep the same machinery on the steady-state signal — an object
to trigger on without transient signals: ``mode`` ``runt`` fires on a pulse that crosses
``low_threshold`` but never ``high_threshold`` (a negative one the mirror below
``high_threshold``), ``transition`` on an edge whose time between the two thresholds fails
``transition_mode`` (``gthan``/``lthan`` against ``transition_time``, ``range``/``orange``
against ``transition_range_low``/``transition_range_high``), ``window`` on the signal entering or leaving the band between
the two thresholds (``window_condition``; ``window_tpoint`` at the boundary instant or after
``window_time`` of staying put, and ``inside``/``outside`` conditions with a ``greater``/
``less`` duration qualifier), ``timeout`` when the signal has stayed high, low or unchanged
for ``timeout_time``, and ``nedge`` on the ``nedge_count``-th edge of the family's slope.
Each family keeps its own ``<family>_source`` (the edge trigger's source until one is set);
the runt, transition and window comparisons read the per-source ``high_threshold``/
``low_threshold`` (``high_by_source``/``low_by_source`` name the sources' settings, like
``level_by_source``), and the hysteresis band follows ``hysteresis_setting`` — ``normal``,
``nreject`` (the noise-reject band) or ``hsensitivity`` (``hsensitivity_divs``, half the
normal band when unset). An unset threshold leaves runt, transition and window nothing to
compare against: the search finds nothing and a waiting acquisition looks again at the next
command.

scope_vertical.label: 垂直通道
scope_vertical.about: 垂直通道：耦合、带宽、刻度与偏置及其范围。
scope_vertical.about_en: The vertical channel: coupling, bandwidth, scale and offset with their ranges.
scope_vertical.doc:
The vertical channel: coupling, bandwidth, and the scale and offset with their ranges.

Analog first-order filters (physics): AC coupling is a ``ac_corner`` high-pass and the
bandwidth a first-order low-pass at ``bandwidth`` (or ``bw_limit_hz`` when the limit is on).
A scope whose bandwidth is a DSP filter declares its shape with ``response``: ``brickwall``
(flat magnitude, linear phase: ringing on a step), ``gaussian`` (no ringing), ``bessel4`` or
``butterworth4``, -3 dB at the same frequency and with the filter's delay removed.
The ``scale`` (V/div) and ``offset`` (V) are display values; with ``scale_range`` and
``offset_ranges`` a change outside the range is refused with -222 and the old value kept. The
ranges are given at the input connector, i.e. the display values divided by ``probe_ratio``. The input noise is a ``noise_table`` row of the scale: real
scopes' noise rides the vertical setting (the front-end gain sets it at the ADC), so a fixed
input value would leave the coarse divisions far quieter than 1 LSB and averaging could not
resolve more.

The unit's own metrology. Each V/div at the input
connector has its own attenuator and gain stage: ``gain_error_ppm`` (relative) and
``offset_error`` (V at the input) are what this unit adds there — a number, or one per input
V/div, the table a ``deviations`` entry with ``by: {scale: …}`` draws; a scale the table does
not list has no characterized error and contributes 0. ``dac_error_ppm`` is the offset DAC's
gain error, referred to the displayed offset setting: a display offset of V moves the record
by V·(1 + d), i.e. the reading is off by V·d. The vertical runs before the probe (which is a
display conversion), so the errors ride the input path and the DAC term is divided by
``probe_ratio`` here. They sit in signal order — coupling, the attenuator's gain, the bias,
then the bandwidth — and the record shows them, since it is reconstructed with the nominal
scale and offset. ``store`` names a ``calibration_store`` whose coefficients correct the
record digitally, (raw − offset) × gain, keyed by the displayed V/div; :meth:`self_calibrate` writes them for every tabulated scale.

setup_memory.label: 设置存储
setup_memory.about: 保存和调出仪表设置：寄存器、状态文件和设置块。
setup_memory.about_en: Saves and recalls the instrument's settings: registers, state files and setup blocks.
setup_memory.doc:
Save and recall the instrument's settings: registers (``*SAV``/``*RCL``,
``:STORe:SETup``), named state files on the instrument's drives (``MMEMory:STORe:STATe``) and
the setup as a block (``*LRN?``, ``:SYSTem:SETup``).

``registers`` numbered from ``first``; ``register_file`` (``INT:\Settings\STATE_{n}.STA``,
needs ``storage``) keeps each register as a file the MMEMory commands see, else they are kept
beside the instrument's drives. ``exclude`` lists settings a setup leaves out (glob patterns
on the state path). Recalling an empty register raises ``empty_error`` (0: no SCPI error, the
instrument only says so on its screen); a file or block that is not a setup of this model
raises ``bad_setup``. Model limits: a setup holds settings only — arbitrary waveforms, reading
memory and other data are not in it; the power-down state (location 0 on the Trueform) is not
written at the end of a run.

siglent_sdg.label: SDG 波形发生
siglent_sdg.about: SDG2000X 专用的波形、输出、反相、同步等命令。
siglent_sdg.about_en: The SDG2000X's own waveform, output, invert and sync commands.
siglent_sdg.doc: C<n>:BSWV, C<n>:OUTP, C<n>:INVT, C<n>:SYNC, PACP and BUZZ of an SDG2000X.

siglent_sdg_channel_limits.label: SDG 输出范围检查
siglent_sdg_channel_limits.about: SDG2000X 的通道设置在命令之外改动时检查其范围。
siglent_sdg_channel_limits.about_en: Checks an SDG2000X channel's ranges when a setting changes outside a command.
siglent_sdg_channel_limits.doc: Checks a channel's ranges whenever one of its settings changes outside a command (UI, bench).

smu_meter.label: SMU 测量
smu_meter.about: SMU 的电压/电流测量：量程电阻、A/D、NPLC 和读数存储。
smu_meter.about_en: The SMU's V/I meter: range resistors, A/D, NPLC and the reading memory.
smu_meter.doc:
The V/I meter: range resistors, A/D, NPLC and the reading memory handoff.

Readings go through a ``trigger_model`` (the ``sampler`` protocol):
one reading takes its NPLC time plus the source delay; a sweep's points are the readings of one
run, each point's level driving the terminal while the run lasts. The measure side ranges like
the meter core: ``measure_ranges`` (per function: the voltage and current readings), the
manual ``measure_range_voltage`` / ``measure_range_current``, ``measure_autorange`` with the
same hysteresis, and a reading beyond ``overrange`` × full scale reads ``overload_value``.

The bench front panel reads this component's values (``core.voltage`` …), so the SMU
definitions keep naming it ``core``.

smu_output.label: SMU 输出级
smu_output.about: SMU 的 HI/LO 端、远端采样、浮地 LO 和输出继电器。
smu_output.about_en: The SMU's HI/LO, remote sense, floating LO and output relay.
smu_output.doc:
The output stage: HI/LO, remote sense, floating LO and the output relay.

The voltage loop regulates the metered points: ``V(sense_hi) − V(sense_lo)`` with remote sense
on, otherwise the force terminals (``V(hi) − V(lo)``; with ``floating: false`` the LO is bonded
to the bench ground, the model's original behaviour). The current always flows through the
force terminals. A sense terminal left unconnected while remote sense is on makes the reading
operations raise an error (the loop falls back to the force terminals); the bench validator
warns about such a bench.

Not a ``driver`` for bench checks: at its limit it sinks current, so a supply on the same net
is a valid bench (quadrant 2). The control loop it drives holds the mode.

smu_source.label: SMU 源设定
smu_source.about: SMU 源 DAC 的设定：源量程、扫描和量程范围。
smu_source.about_en: The SMU source DAC's setting: source range, sweep and range envelope.
smu_source.doc:
The source DAC's setting: source range, the sweep, and the range envelope.

It stamps no circuit element. The control loop takes the level from its own bindings and the
output stage turns the loop's target into a circuit source; this component owns the *ranges*:
``source_ranges`` (full-scale values per function) with ``range_limits`` (the cap the other
quantity's limit gets on each range, the 21 V / 105 mA boundary by default), and the sweep
(linear, logarithmic or list) that drives a run's levels. The control loop asks it to cap a
limit for the level in use (:meth:`limit_cap`), so the envelope follows a sweep point too.

specan_ddc.label: 数字下变频
specan_ddc.about: 把 ADC 样本搬到零中频并抽取，输出复基带样本。
specan_ddc.about_en: Shifts the ADC's samples to 0 Hz and decimates them into complex baseband.
specan_ddc.doc:
The digital down-converter: the ADC's samples times a numerically
controlled oscillator at ``nco_hz`` — the intermediate frequency comes to 0 Hz — then the
decimation filter and the lower rate. ``out`` carries complex baseband samples (``iq``) whose
0 Hz stands for the frequency the receiver is tuned to (the frame's ``center_hz``); a real tone
of amplitude A on the IF is the complex amplitude A.

``decimation`` 0 is automatic: the block runs at the rate asked of it, a whole number of ADC
samples per output sample (the resolution filter behind it asks for a rate that follows the
RBW). The filter is a Kaiser-windowed sinc with ``stopband`` dB of attenuation
(:func:`decimation_taps`): flat over the middle half of the output rate, which is the band a
reader may use; its length is ``taps_per_phase(stopband)`` output intervals, and that history —
one tap less than its length, in ADC samples — is the warm-up it asks the ADC for ahead of
every frame. A decimation of 1 has no filter and no warm-up.

The oscillator is a number of cycles per ADC sample, so it runs off the ADC's clock: an error
of the reference moves it with the sample rate, and the frequency scale of everything behind
it carries that error once, as the swept analyzer's does.

specan_detector.label: 检波
specan_detector.about: 每个分辨单元的检波方式（峰值、采样、平均、RMS 等）与对数换算。
specan_detector.about_en: The detector per resolution cell (peak, sample, average, RMS, …) and log conversion.
specan_detector.doc:
The detector and log conversion: positive peak / sample / average / RMS / negative
peak / normal per resolution cell, then the level in dBm.

Normal (Rosenfell) shows the peak of a CW-like bucket; a noise-like bucket (its cells
spread by more than ``normal_spread``) shows the maximum on even points and the minimum on odd
ones, as the X-Series reference describes. With ``auto`` the detector follows the trace mode:
max hold peak, min hold negative peak, otherwise normal (the X-Series preset rule); a detector
chosen through :meth:`op_select` turns ``auto`` off.

specan_if.label: 中频滤波
specan_if.about: ADC 前的中频滤波与放大，防止混叠。
specan_if.about_en: The IF filter and amplifier ahead of the ADC, which keeps it from aliasing.
specan_if.doc:
The IF filter and amplifier: the analog passband ahead of the ADC —
what keeps the converter from aliasing — centered on the intermediate frequency ``if_hz``,
``bandwidth`` wide at -3 dB, and the IF gain. ``out`` is the mixer's output through it.

The passband is maximally flat (a Butterworth magnitude of order 5, no phase): within 0.03 dB
over the middle 60 % of the bandwidth, 30 dB down at twice the bandwidth. The resolution
bandwidth is not here: it is the digital filter behind the ADC (``specan_rbw``).

specan_input.label: 输入衰减器
specan_input.about: 频谱仪的输入步进衰减器和过载检查。
specan_input.about_en: The analyzer's input step attenuator and overload check.
specan_input.doc:
The input attenuator and overload check: the RF input port is the generic
``input_port`` (50 Ω to ground, the only circuit-layer part of the analyzer). The step
attenuator is automatic (reference level kept at the mixer limit, 2 dB steps) or manual; the
receiver overloads when the total input power minus the attenuation passes the maximum mixer
level. ``out`` is the input attenuated (and amplified by the preamplifier, 0 dB unless
declared).

specan_lo.label: 本振
specan_lo.about: 本振：接收机调谐到哪里、频率参考和扫描速度。
specan_lo.about_en: The local oscillator: where the receiver is tuned, its reference and sweep speed.
specan_lo.doc:
The local oscillator: where the receiver is tuned, the reference its
frequency runs off, and how fast it sweeps.

The tuning point is the frequency whose signal the mixer puts on the IF: the one of the read
in progress (``Session.tuned``, set by the trace or an internal probe), else the center
